newsitem.title: USA: jurors say they are making progress in ABC case.
newsitem.headline: jurors say they are making progress in ABC case.

text.p: Jurors began a sixth day of deliberations on Wednesday to decide whether ABC television network will pay punitive damages to supermarket chain Food Lion Inc. for a hidden camera report on the grocer.
The jury of six men and six women, which had been at an impasse, told the judge late Tuesday that it was finally making progress in its deliberations.

Food Lion sued ABC and four of its producers for a 1992 hidden-camera investigation that claimed the supermarket chain sold old meat and fish and its food-handling was unsantiary. The grocery chain has not challenged the truth of the report, but filed a lawsuit accusing ABC of fraud by having two journalists break the law to to get jobs with Food Lion.
The programme aired on ABC's PrimeTime Live programme on Nov. 5, 1992.

Food Lion lawyers last week urged the jury to order ABC to pay "very large" damages for the programme -- so large that the network, and others, would be deterred from conducting future hidden-camera reports that break the law in the process.

The jury hearing the case in U.S. District Court in Greensboro, N.C., found last month that ABC committed fraud, trespass and breach of loyalty when two television journalists worked undercover at different Food Lion stores. The panel awarded the grocer about $1,400 in actual damages.
ABC is a unit of Walt Disney Co.
